goal: Rebuild web/map.html in place as an interactive, pannable and zoomable "city" of Claude Code sessions whose geography derives from identity rather than status, with a live agent roster and per-agent modals offering stats, conversation, chat and kill — on a feed and a renderer that cost nothing when nothing is happening, with no build step and no dependency.

entries.title: Feed: idle-aware refresh, visibility-paused polling, conditional responses
entries.description:
Reduce the standing cost of `ccwatch serve` so the interactive map that follows is built on a feed that does not bill for itself when nobody is watching.

Measured 2026-09-07 on a host with 18 live sessions: one `ccwatch --json` snapshot takes **~2.1s warm** (`collect_host` 549ms, `collect_sessions` 499ms, `collect_repos` 495ms, remainder ~570ms) and **~24s on a cold cache under load** (`collect_repos` 7562ms, `collect_host` 7003ms, `collect_sessions` 4737ms). The refresher at `bin/ccwatch:2735-2747` runs it as `while True: run(); time.sleep(2)`, so `serve` holds roughly a **50% duty cycle of one core for as long as it is open**, whether or not any page is open. That, and not the drawing technology, is the resource cost of this tool.

What it must do:

1. **Idle-aware refresh.** The snapshot refresher stops collecting when no client has fetched `/api/state` within a short grace period, and resumes on the next request. Keep the existing architecture's principle — one refresher, N readers, the handler never blocks (`bin/ccwatch:2696-2707`) — and keep the three independent refreshers separate for the reason already recorded there (`bin/ccwatch:2724-2734`): a slow collector may only make its own panel stale. The `deploys` (60s) and `peers` (45s) refreshers get the same idle gating. The first request after an idle period must never present a resumed-from snapshot as current: it reports warming, or it reports the measured age (constitution III).

2. **Conditional responses.** `/api/state` carries a strong validator (an ETag over the serialised payload) and answers a matching `If-None-Match` with `304`, so an unchanged snapshot costs the page no parse and no DOM work. Note the header today is `Cache-Control: no-store` (`bin/ccwatch:2925`), which forbids the storage a 304 revalidation depends on; `no-cache` is the header that means what is wanted here — stored, but never used without revalidating. Getting this wrong yields either a permanently-200 endpoint or a page showing a cached snapshot as live, and the second is a constitution III violation.

3. **The client pauses when it is not being read.** Both `web/index.html` and `web/map.html` stop polling when `document.visibilityState === "hidden"` and resume on `visibilitychange`, fetching once immediately on return so what a person sees when they come back is not the snapshot from before they left. A hidden background tab currently costs a full collection every ~2s indefinitely.

4. **No animation loop anywhere on either page.** Rendering is event-driven — a data change, a camera change, hover, or focus. No `requestAnimationFrame` loop and no repainting `setInterval`. CSS animation is permitted only on figures whose motion carries a signal (working, blocked, suspect), never as decoration, and stays subject to `prefers-reduced-motion`. This is what keeps the page at zero CPU between ticks, and it is the constraint that rules out a game-loop renderer for the entries that follow.

5. **The snapshot timeout tail.** The 40s ceiling (`bin/ccwatch:2943`) against a measured 24s cold path is a thin margin. When it is crossed, `run()` returns `{"error": ...}`, `snapshot_ok` converts that to an empty `sessions` list, and the map renders it as "No live sessions" (`web/map.html:649-651`) — which is the reported "agents vanish with no explanation" bug, arriving from the server side. Make the ceiling adequate or configurable, and make a timed-out or failed snapshot **distinguishable in the payload** from a run that genuinely found nothing (constitution IV). The rendering of that distinction belongs to `map-stable-world`; this entry is responsible for the payload carrying the fact.

6. **Measure it and state the numbers.** Record before and after in `README.md`: the duty cycle with a page open, with the tab hidden, and with no client at all. The concrete measured figure, not an adjective — as the existing comments in this file do.

7. **No new dependency, no build step, no new endpoint.** bash 3.2 forms only; `python3 -c`, never on stdin; `shellcheck -x -S warning` clean for `bin/ccwatch` and `tests/run.sh`; `./tests/run.sh` the only test entry point.

8. **Tests.** Hermetic under `$WORK` via `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` with `CCWATCH_FAKE_PS`. The idle gating, the 304 behaviour, and the timed-out-versus-empty distinction are each worth an assertion. Mutation-check every one (break the implementation in the specific way the assertion describes, confirm it fails, restore), add a row each to the mutation table in `README.md`, and raise `TALLY_FLOOR`. Reap any `serve` a test starts — a leaked one holds a port a later run may pick. Prefer `t_skip` with a stated reason over a flake on a slow machine.

What this entry must NOT take on: nothing about the map's drawing model, layout, camera, roster or modal — those are the four entries after this one, and this entry must leave both pages looking exactly as they do now apart from the pause-when-hidden behaviour. Do not change what any collector computes, and do not add or alter a status, severity or verdict. Do not weaken the per-run send token or the `Origin` check (constitution IX), and do not remove or soften any staleness withholding (constitution III).
entries.rationale: First because it is small, independently valuable, and changes the environment every later entry is built in. The map entries add a client that polls a feed; building them against a feed that collects continuously bakes in exactly the cost that must be avoided, and retrofitting an event-driven renderer onto a page that already has an animation loop is more work than starting without one. It also lands the payload-side half of the "agents vanish with no explanation" bug — a timed-out snapshot must be distinguishable from an empty one before any view can render the difference — which is why it precedes `map-stable-world` rather than following it. Depends on nothing.

entries.title: Map: identity-derived world layout, incremental rendering, four distinct failure states
entries.description:
Rebuild the drawing model of `web/map.html` (replace the existing /map — do not add a third page) so that the city's geography is derived from identity and never re-flows, and so a tick that fails does not empty the map.

What it must do:

1. **One world space.** Replace the `#map` CSS grid (`web/map.html:46`) and the per-tick `innerHTML` replacement (`web/map.html:649`) with a single `<svg>` containing one `<g>` camera group. Hierarchy inside it: GitHub org = district, repo = building, branch = a zone within the building, session = a figure inside the building. The org comes from splitting the existing `repo` field (`owner/name`) in the payload — no collection-side change is needed for it. A directory with no git remote gets its own `no repo` district and is never folded into a real org (constitution VI); it must be visibly labelled as such, as the current `.norepo` badge does.

2. **Position derives from identity, never from status.** Coordinates come from a deterministic function of the identity strings (org, `owner/name` or the directory key for a remote-less project, branch, `sid`) — a stable hash, not an index into a status-sorted list. Assignments are persisted in localStorage so a plot a person has learned stays put across reloads, and a newly appearing repo lands in free space by the same deterministic placement without moving anything already placed. Nothing volatile — `sev`, `psev`, `quiet`, `waited`, `token`, deploy state — may feed a coordinate or a spatial ordering. Delete the per-tick severity re-sort at `web/map.html:643-647`; the comment at `web/map.html:613-615` already claims the behaviour this entry actually delivers.

3. **Incremental rendering.** Diff the payload by `sid` (and by building/zone key) and create, update or remove nodes per tick. No code on the tick path may replace a container's `innerHTML` wholesale. An open inspector, a hover, a text selection and the viewport must survive a 3s refresh.

4. **Peer wires in world coordinates.** The wires are today positioned from measured DOM rects (`web/map.html:359-392`), which cannot survive any camera transform. Move them inside the camera group and compute them from world coordinates. Keep what they already say: bowed paths so A→B and B→A are two lines, the arrowhead, the count bubble only when `count > 1`, edges drawn only when both ends are on the map, and the footer note reporting `drawn/total` when some edges involve sessions that have exited.

5. **Four distinct failure renderings** (constitution III, IV). A feed that is down (fetch or HTTP failure), a snapshot still warming (`warming: true`), registry rows that could not be read, and a genuine absence of sessions are four different facts and must read as four different sentences. In the first three the buildings and districts stay drawn, the map is marked stale with the measured age from `ages.snapshot`, and the volatile readings are **withheld** — the context fill inside a figure, percentages, memory figures — rather than left on screen looking current. `if (s.warming) return` (`web/map.html:610`) must go: it leaves the previous DOM standing with only a footer note. An empty `sessions` array must not be rendered as "No live sessions" when the payload also carries a snapshot `error`.

6. **Surface the unreadable-rows count in the payload** so state 3 above is a fact read rather than inferred. `PARSE_FAILED` is currently a shell variable (`bin/ccwatch:184`) that only reaches the terminal footer (`bin/ccwatch:1139`); add it to the snapshot JSON so `ccwatch --json` and `/api/state` carry the same number the terminal prints, and render it from the payload. No status, severity or verdict may be derived in JS (constitution XI).

7. **Camera is static in this entry.** Compute the world bounds and fit them into the SVG viewBox (or the camera transform) once per layout change, and on resize. This must be genuinely usable on its own: the whole city visible, figures legible.

8. **Keep everything the page does today working.** The existing inspector (`#reply` — ask panel, conversation, send box, kill bar) still opens on a figure click and still works. Gauges with their staleness withholding, the host-pressure line (absent below the threshold — constitution XII), the legend, the footer, the counts and the document title all keep their current behaviour and wording. Motion stays meaning-bearing and `prefers-reduced-motion` stays honoured. Every figure state keeps a distinct word available as text, not colour alone (constitution VII). Preserve the literal source line `const SEND_TOKEN = "__CCWATCH_SEND_TOKEN__";` — an existing assertion in `tests/run.sh` greps the served *map* page for the injected token and will break if that line is reshaped.

9. **No build step, no dependency, no CDN fetch, no new endpoint.** Static HTML with inline CSS and JS, as now. bash 3.2 forms only for any script change; `shellcheck -x -S warning` clean; `./tests/run.sh` is the only test entry point.

10. **Tests.** Hermetic assertions under `$WORK` via `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` with `CCWATCH_FAKE_PS` — never against live sessions. The unreadable-rows field is a server-side behaviour and must be asserted as one. Mutation-check every new assertion (break the implementation in the specific way it describes, confirm it fails, restore), add a row per mutation to the table in `README.md`, and raise `TALLY_FLOOR`. Prefer `t_skip` with a stated reason over a flake. Update the `README.md` map section: it currently describes the responsive grid as the design, and must instead document the identity-derived geography and name the three bugs this entry fixes.

What this entry must NOT take on: interactive pan and zoom, semantic level-of-detail and persisted viewport belong to `map-camera-lod`; the roster panel belongs to `map-roster`; replacing the inspector with a per-agent modal, and making the `--allow-kill` gate visible as a disabled button, belong to `map-agent-modal`. Do not add a status, severity, verdict or badge that the payload does not already carry.

11. **Event-driven, sprite-ready drawing (footprint).** The renderer runs on events only — a data change, a hover, a focus — with no `requestAnimationFrame` loop and no repainting `setInterval`, preserving what `feed-footprint` established. A figure, a building and a district are each drawn through **one swappable primitive**, so a later change of art direction touches that primitive and not the layout: the world is laid out in integer world units, sprite rendering is prepared for (`image-rendering: pixelated`, an `<image>`-or-CSS-sprite seam at the primitive boundary, a single atlas if one is ever added), but this entry ships simple pixel-styled shapes drawn in SVG and adds **no image asset, no CDN reference and no binary to the repository**. Motion remains signal-bearing only — a working, blocked or suspect figure may animate in CSS, an idle one does not (constitution XII) — and `prefers-reduced-motion` is honoured. No game-loop or canvas framework, and no new runtime dependency of any kind.
entries.rationale: First because everything else is drawn on top of it. Pan and zoom need a single transformed world space to transform; the roster needs stable figures to fly a camera to; the modal needs a render that does not destroy it every 3 seconds. It also carries the highest uncertainty in the whole roadmap — the coordinate derivation, the localStorage placement, and moving the peer wires off measured DOM rects — so resolving it first stops the later entries being designed against a layout that turns out not to work. The wires move here rather than later because introducing the camera group without them breaks a feature that works today. Depends on nothing before it.

entries.title: Map: pan, zoom, semantic level-of-detail, persisted viewport
entries.description:
Turn the static fitted view from `map-stable-world` into a navigable camera over the same world space.

What it must do:

1. **Pan and zoom on the one transform.** Wheel/trackpad zoom anchored at the cursor, drag to pan, and on-screen controls. Zoom limits and pan clamped to the world bounds so the city cannot be lost off-screen. Resize must not lose the current position.

2. **Operable without a mouse** (constitution VII): arrow keys pan, `+`/`-` zoom, `0` fits the whole world, and the controls are real focusable buttons with labels. A trackpad pinch gesture is welcome but is not the accessible path.

3. **Zoom is semantic, not merely scale.** Three levels of detail: *far* — districts with a count and the worst status they contain; *mid* — buildings with their branch zones; *near* — individual figures with names and current activity. Level is chosen from the camera scale with hysteresis, so a tick or a one-pixel wheel event cannot flip it back and forth. **Level of detail may change what is drawn and how much of it, never a coordinate** — a building sits in the same place at every zoom. The counts and worst-status shown at far zoom are read from the payload's `sev`/`psev`, not recomputed (constitution XI), and each carries its distinguishing word, not only a colour.

4. **Persist the viewport** (pan and zoom) in localStorage and restore it on reload, with a first-run default of fit-to-world and a visible reset/fit control. A restored viewport that no longer intersects any content must fall back to fit rather than opening on empty ground.

5. **Wires and figures stay legible under transform.** Wire stroke widths, arrowheads, count bubbles and any text must not become hairlines or giants as scale changes (non-scaling stroke, or counter-scaled text). The wires already live in world coordinates after the first entry; this entry is responsible for their appearance across the zoom range.

6. **Everything from the previous entry keeps working:** identity-derived positions, incremental diffing, the four distinct failure states with the geography retained, the existing inspector, gauges, host-pressure line, legend, counts, footer. A failure state must be readable at whatever zoom the person left the camera at.

7. Static page, no build step, no dependency, no new endpoint. New assertions hermetic and mutation-checked, a row each in the `README.md` mutation table, `TALLY_FLOOR` raised. Document in `README.md` what each zoom level shows and why level-of-detail is semantic rather than a scale factor.

What this entry must NOT take on: the roster panel and camera fly-to-on-select belong to `map-roster` — expose whatever camera API (centre-on-world-point, animated, with a reduced-motion jump) that entry will need, but do not build the panel. The per-agent modal and the visible `--allow-kill` gate belong to `map-agent-modal`. Do not change the payload, add an endpoint, or introduce a new status or severity.

8. **Discrete zoom steps, and no per-frame JavaScript (footprint).** Zoom moves in discrete integer-friendly steps rather than continuously, which is what keeps a future sprite atlas crisp and what gives the three levels of detail an unambiguous boundary — the pixel-art constraint and the level-of-detail constraint want the same thing here. Pan and zoom are applied as a transform on the single camera group so the compositor does the work; a camera move must not re-render the scene graph or run JavaScript per frame, and it must not touch the poll cadence or the visibility pause from `feed-footprint`. Any easing on a camera move is a bounded CSS or Web-Animations transition that ends, not a loop, and reduces to an instant jump under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
entries.rationale: Second because it depends on the single world-space transform and the world-coordinate wires that `map-stable-world` establishes, and because the roster's fly-to is meaningless without a camera to fly. It comes before the roster and the modal because it is the remaining piece of spatial uncertainty: whether the level-of-detail thresholds and the persisted viewport hold up decides how much the roster and the modal have to do about navigation, and both are easier to specify once the camera API exists.

entries.title: Map: docked agent roster, severity-sorted, keyboard navigable, camera fly-to
entries.description:
Add the docked roster panel that owns all volatile ordering and serves as the map's textual representation.

What it must do:

1. **Every active agent, always visible.** A docked list beside the map with one row per session in the payload. Each row carries the session name, its repo and branch (or `no repo`), the status **word**, and the measurement that justified it (constitution II) — the silence or the waited time, the pipeline phase and status, context percentage, memory — with stale volatile readings withheld rather than annotated (constitution III).

2. **Sorted "needs you" first**, from the payload's `sev` and `psev`. Severity sorting is correct *here* and wrong on the map: a list is expected to be ordered, a spatial arrangement is expected to be remembered (constitution XIII). No severity or verdict is computed in the panel; it sorts and formats what the payload says (constitution XI).

3. **The accessible representation of the map** (constitution VII). Every claim a figure draws — pose, colour, halo, animation, context fill — must be reachable as text in the roster. The SVG city is presented as a decorative or labelled companion to it rather than as the only carrier of meaning. Rows are focusable, navigable with the keyboard (up/down, Enter to select, Home/End), and correctly labelled for a screen reader.

4. **Selecting a row selects the agent**: the row is marked selected, the corresponding figure is emphasised on the map, and the camera flies to it using the API from `map-camera-lod` — animated, but a direct jump under `prefers-reduced-motion`. Selection is persisted in localStorage and survives ticks. If the selected session is gone from a tick, say so in the row's place rather than silently dropping the selection — and distinguish that from the feed being down.

5. **The four failure states read here too**, in four different sentences: the feed is down, the snapshot is warming, N registry rows could not be read (with the `ccwatch doctor` pointer the terminal footer gives), and there are genuinely no live sessions. When the feed is down or warming, the roster must not present its last-known rows as current.

6. **Roster width is resizable and persisted**, and the panel must be usable at a narrow viewport without hiding the status word or its measurement.

7. **Nothing about the terminal changes.** `ccwatch once | grep HUNG` keeps working unchanged; no CLI rendering or payload change belongs in this entry. Keep the map behaviours from the two previous entries intact, including the existing inspector on a figure click.

8. Static page, no build step, no dependency. New assertions hermetic and mutation-checked, a row each in the `README.md` mutation table, `TALLY_FLOOR` raised. Document in `README.md` why volatile ordering lives in the roster and not on the map, naming the re-orientation bug that motivated it.

What this entry must NOT take on: the per-agent modal — stats, conversation, chat and kill — belongs to `map-agent-modal`; until then, selecting a roster row selects and flies the camera, and the existing `#reply` inspector remains what opens for reading and replying. Do not add an endpoint, and do not add a status or severity the payload does not carry.
entries.rationale: Third because the fly-to-on-select behaviour that makes the roster more than a sidebar needs the camera from `map-camera-lod`, and because rows must key off the same identity and diffing model `map-stable-world` established. It comes before the modal because it establishes the selection state and the text formatting of every session's stats — which the modal then reuses rather than inventing a second time — and because it is what discharges the accessibility obligation for the graphical city, so the modal is not the only path to a figure's meaning.

entries.title: Map: per-agent modal with stats, conversation, chat, and a visible kill gate
entries.description:
Replace the existing `#reply` inspector with a per-agent modal, opened from a figure click or from a roster row, and make the kill capability visible when it is disabled.

What it must do:

1. **Stats from the row it was opened from.** Status word plus the measurement behind it, silence or waited time, age, context percentage, memory, pipeline phase and status, repo, branch, session id, and the peer edges touching this session. All read from the `/api/state` row — nothing recomputed in JS (constitution XI) — with stale volatile readings withheld rather than annotated (constitution III), and the whole panel kept current as ticks arrive, including a pending question that has since been answered elsewhere.

2. **Conversation** from `/api/transcript`, keeping the existing bounded and redacted treatment exactly: a bounded byte tail, assistant/user text truncated, a tool *use* reduced to its name and a short argument summary, a tool *result* reduced to its size and never its content (constitution X). Keep the slower poll cadence while open and the scroll behaviour that only follows when already at the bottom.

3. **The pending-ask panel** keeps its current prominence and, verbatim in meaning, its statement that a dialog can only be answered in that session's own terminal and that a message sent from here is queued *behind* it rather than answering it. Keep the distinct treatment of a waiting session with no recorded question.

4. **Chat/reply** via `/api/send`, reporting the three observed outcomes — delivered, queued, failed with the real reason (constitution VIII). Keep the per-run token header and the server's `Origin` check; neither may be weakened because the other exists (constitution IX). Under `--read-only` the send control is shown disabled with the reason, not hidden.

5. **Kill, with the gate made visible.** Killing stays gated on `ccwatch serve --allow-kill` server-side; nothing about the endpoint or its refusals changes. But when `can_kill` is false the modal renders a **disabled** kill button naming the flag that would enable it, because today the whole control is omitted (`web/map.html:502-543`, gated on `s.can_kill`) and a capability absent from the UI reads as a feature that was never built (constitution IV). When it is enabled, keep the existing double-confirm, the "frees NMB" figure taken from the same snapshot the map drew, the pipeline-phase and mid-turn warnings, the `claude --resume <sid>` hint, and the verbatim refusal text — a refusal explains what would have been lost and must not be flattened to "failed".

6. **It behaves like a modal.** Focus moves into it on open and is trapped while it is open, Escape closes it, focus returns to whatever opened it, and it survives the 3s tick without losing an in-progress message, a scroll position or a confirmation step. Opening is reachable from both a figure and a roster row, by keyboard as well as pointer.

7. **The rest of the map keeps working:** identity-derived positions, camera and level-of-detail, persisted viewport, the roster and its selection, and the four distinct failure states — including inside the modal, which must say that the feed is down rather than showing its last figures as current.

8. Static page, no build step, no dependency, and no new endpoint: `/api/send`, `/api/kill` and `/api/transcript` are the ones that exist and are the ones used. New assertions hermetic and mutation-checked (the disabled-kill-button-when-ungated behaviour is one worth an assertion of its own), a row each in the `README.md` mutation table, `TALLY_FLOOR` raised. Update `README.md` to document the modal and to state why a disabled kill button with the flag named beats an absent one.

What this entry must NOT take on: no changes to kill semantics, to the server's `--allow-kill` gate, to the token or `Origin` checks, or to the transcript redaction rules — this is the view over them. No new endpoint, no new status or severity, and no further change to the layout, camera or roster beyond what opening and closing the modal requires. This is the last entry in the roadmap; nothing may be deferred past it.
entries.rationale: Last because it is the only entry that depends on all three before it: it is opened from the figures `map-stable-world` draws and reached from the roster rows `map-roster` builds, it reuses that entry's stats formatting, and it needs the incremental render for a modal to survive a tick at all. It is also the entry with the least uncertainty — the send, kill and transcript endpoints and their gates already exist and are unchanged — so it is the right thing to do once the spatial and ordering questions are settled. The visible `--allow-kill` gate lands here rather than earlier because it belongs to the modal that replaces the current inspector, and moving it earlier would mean building that control twice.
